lesson.title: Improper Fractions and Mixed Numbers: Two Ways to Say the Same Thing

steps.say: Imagine it's pizza night in Vancouver, and you and your family order pizzas cut into quarters. After everyone eats, there are seven quarter-slices left in the boxes. Seven quarters! But when your friend asks how much pizza is left, you probably wouldn't say seven quarters. You'd say one whole pizza and three quarters. Both answers are exactly the same amount. That's what today's lesson is all about.

visual.caption: Seven quarter-slices = one whole pizza plus three quarters

steps.say: Let's name our two ways of talking. When the top number is bigger than the bottom number, like seven quarters, we call it an improper fraction. Improper just means the top is heavy, more than one whole. When we say one and three quarters, that's a mixed number, because it mixes a whole number with a fraction. Nothing is wrong with either one. They're just two outfits for the same amount.

visual.caption: Seven shaded quarters, drawn as one full bar and part of a second

steps.say: Here's the little trick to go from an improper fraction to a mixed number. The bottom number tells you how many pieces make one whole. So with seven quarters, ask yourself: how many groups of four can I pull out of seven? Just one group of four, and three pieces are left over. So seven quarters is one whole and three quarters left. Divide, and the leftover becomes the fraction part.

visual.caption: Seven pieces make one group of four, with three left over

steps.say: Let's try one together. Ms. Yuanyuan baked banana bread and cut each loaf into three equal pieces. She counts eleven pieces on the tray. How many whole loaves is that? Three pieces make one loaf, so we ask how many threes fit into eleven. Three, six, nine — that's three loaves — and eleven take away nine leaves two pieces over. So eleven thirds is three and two thirds loaves.

visual.caption: Eleven pieces make three groups of three, with two pieces left over

steps.say: Now let's go the other way, from a mixed number back to an improper fraction. Say you have two and three fifths litres of apple juice. Each litre is five fifths. So two whole litres is two times five, which is ten fifths, and then add the extra three fifths. Ten plus three is thirteen. So two and three fifths equals thirteen fifths. Multiply the whole by the bottom, then add the top.

visual.caption: Thirteen fifths sits between two and three, at two and three fifths

steps.say: A number line is a lovely way to check yourself. Where does nine quarters live? Four quarters make one, eight quarters make two, so nine quarters is just one quarter past two. That's two and one quarter. Whenever the top is bigger than the bottom, the number lands past one on the line — that's your clue it's an improper fraction.

visual.caption: Nine quarters lands one quarter past the number two

steps.say: Here's where this really helps. Which is more: five halves of a chocolate bar, or two and one quarter bars? Turn the improper one into a mixed number first. Five halves means five divided by two, which is two with one half left, so two and one half. Now compare two and one half with two and one quarter. Same two wholes, but one half is bigger than one quarter. So five halves wins. Changing the outfit made the comparison easy.

visual.caption: Two and one quarter jumps up to two and one half — five halves is bigger

steps.say: So remember: an improper fraction and a mixed number are the same amount wearing different clothes. To go from improper to mixed, divide and keep the leftover on top. To go back, multiply the whole by the bottom and add the top. Pick whichever one makes your job easier!

lesson.answer: An improper fraction and a mixed number are the same amount in different clothes: divide to go one way, multiply-and-add to come back.

practice.question: Ms. Yuanyuan has 3 and 2 fifths litres of milk in the fridge for hot chocolate. Write that amount as an improper fraction. Then, at the farmers market she buys 17 fifths of a kilogram of blueberries — write that as a mixed number.
practice.answer: 3 and 2 fifths litres = (3 × 5 + 2) fifths = 17/5 litres. And 17/5 kg = 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2 = 3 and 2 fifths kg. (They're the same pair of numbers, just flipped — 17/5 and 3 2/5 are equal.)
